_: One entry per community board the app can run as (?board=cb3). Committee names match what each board's minutes call them, so a past resolution's committee can be picked again. Read by worker/index.ts and the build scripts.

cb2.name: CB2 Manhattan
cb2.areas: Greenwich Village, West Village, SoHo, NoHo, Hudson Square, Little Italy and part of Chinatown

committees.SLA – 1: Bars, restaurants and venues with liquor licenses, mostly in the eastern part of CB2 (SoHo, NoHo, Little Italy, Chinatown, the Bowery): noise and music from licensed premises, hours, crowds, new or renewed liquor licenses, and their sidewalk and roadway cafés.
committees.SLA – 2: Bars, restaurants and venues with liquor licenses, mostly in the western part of CB2 (West Village, Greenwich Village, Hudson Square, Gansevoort): noise and music from licensed premises, hours, crowds, new or renewed liquor licenses, and their sidewalk and roadway cafés.
committees.Cannabis Licensing Committee: Cannabis dispensaries and smoke shops: licensing, unlicensed sales, location near schools.
committees.Street Activities & Resiliency: Street fairs, block parties, sidewalk vendors, film shoots, sanitation and garbage on streets, flooding and climate resiliency.
committees.Outdoor Dining Working Group: The Dining Out NYC program as a whole: its rules, enforcement and abandoned sheds. Not one restaurant's sidewalk or roadway café; those go to SLA when the place has a liquor license, else to Land Use & Housing.
committees.Traffic & Transportation: Streets, bike lanes, crosswalks, traffic signals, bus routes, parking, speeding, truck traffic, Citi Bike, pedestrian safety.
committees.Parks & Waterfront: Parks, playgrounds, Washington Square Park, Hudson River Park, trees and green space, park hours and conduct.
committees.Landmarks & Public Aesthetics: Changes to buildings in historic districts: facades, windows, signage, storefronts, rooftop additions, public art.
committees.Land Use & Housing: Zoning, new development, construction projects, affordable housing, tenant issues, SoHo/NoHo rezoning, and sidewalk or roadway café applications from places without a liquor license.
committees.Human Services: Homelessness, shelters, mental health, seniors, public health, social services.
committees.Schools & Education: Public schools, school siting and space, education programs, libraries.
committees.Arts & Culture Working Group: Arts organizations, cultural events, galleries, performance spaces.
committees.Community Facilities Advisory Panel: Community facility uses such as houses of worship, medical facilities, and nonprofit spaces in buildings.
committees.Executive Committee: Board-wide policy, budget priorities, or issues that span several committees or fit no other committee.

examples.ex: I'm a parent at PS 3. We need a crossing guard at Hudson St and Christopher St, cars run the light every morning at drop-off.
We want the board's support for a public mural and performance series in Hudson Square
Washington Square Park should not close at night.
Our middle school needs to expand into the empty floor of its building and I want the board's support
I live above the bar at 2 Bleecker St. They leave the windows wide open until 1am and I can hear everything in my bedroom.
The street light in front of 60 Spring St has been out for a week

cb3.name: CB3 Manhattan
cb3.areas: the East Village, Lower East Side and Chinatown

committees.SLA Licensing & Outdoor Dining: Bars, restaurants and venues with liquor licenses anywhere in CB3: noise and music from licensed premises, hours, crowds, new or renewed liquor licenses, sidewalk and roadway dining.
committees.Transportation, Public Safety, Sanitatio: Streets, bike lanes, crosswalks, traffic signals, bus stops and intercity buses, parking, street co-namings, block parties, street fairs and parades, police and public safety, garbage, sanitation and the environment.
committees.Parks, Recreation, Waterfront, & Resilie: Parks and playgrounds, Tompkins Square Park, East River Park, the waterfront, trees and green space, flood and climate resiliency.
committees.Land Use, Zoning, Public & Private Housi: Zoning, new development, construction, affordable housing, NYCHA, tenant issues, and city-owned sites and their tenants: Essex Market, Essex Crossing and the Market Line.
committees.Landmarks: Any work on a landmarked building or site or in a historic district: facades, windows, signage, storefronts, rooftop additions, accessibility lifts, gardens or open space on a landmarked lot, and upkeep plans tied to a landmark selling its air rights.
committees.Health, Seniors & Human Services / Youth: Homelessness and shelters, mental health, addiction services and the buildings of social-service providers, seniors (including discounts or programs for seniors), public health, schools, youth programs, human rights, immigrants and sanctuary-city policy.
committees.Economic Development: Small businesses, commercial rents and storefronts, street vendors, jobs.
committees.Cannabis Control Task Force: Cannabis dispensaries and smoke shops: licensing, unlicensed sales, location near schools, and changes to a dispensary such as a service window or hours.
committees.Executive: Board-wide policy and the board's own rules, open container waivers, or issues that fit no other committee. A proposed law goes to the committee for its topic.

examples.ex: We want the board's support to make St Marks Pl between 2nd and 3rd Ave an open street on weekends.
Tompkins Square Park should get more shade trees and benches along Avenue A.
We want the board's support for a weekend night market for local vendors on Orchard St.
The board should back expanding the senior center on Grand St so it can serve more lunches.
The bar at 117 Avenue A keeps its front doors open after 10pm and the music fills my apartment.
The street light in front of 228 Mott St has been out for a week
